description: Schema for the English Coach lesson-block system. A lesson is DATA: an ordered list of typed blocks. The runtime composer selects/orders blocks by learner context and renders each by looking its `type` up in a component registry. Every block carries a `zone` (placement) and a `role` (semantic color).

accentDashed.use: an active task the learner must complete

warning.use: the learner's diagnosed error / due items

note: `--accent` is set on the screen root to the skill's bucket token (e.g. --b-punct), so accent-role blocks always read as the current skill's color. role→color is resolved at render time.

rule.whenToUse: Always available. The one-line rule + optional worked/anti examples. The reference spine of any lesson.

fields.title: string  — eyebrow label, e.g. 'The rule, in one line'
fields.examples: Array<{ text: string, note: string, kind: 'good' | 'bad' }>?  — ✓ good / ✕ counter examples

workedExample.whenToUse: First exposure or rebuild. A fully-worked model — ALL steps shown (scaffold ●●●). Pair with completionTry (alternation).

fields.title: string
fields.steps: string[]   — every reasoning step, shown in full
fields.answer: string    — the resolved conclusion (rendered as a success chip)

completionTry.whenToUse: Immediately after a workedExample — backward-faded practice (●●○): the learner completes the back-end. Ends the teach loop on a doable win.

fields.title: string
fields.promptHint: string  — nudge toward the missing final step (never the answer)

annotatedExample.whenToUse: Quick visual refresher. One canonical item marked up with color-signaled callouts showing WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE. Lowest text, highest clarity.

fields.title: string
fields.examples: Array<{ pre: string, clause: string, post: string, essential: boolean, callouts: string[] }>  — non-essential clause = accent tint + commas shown; essential = muted tint + no commas

misconceptionCallout.whenToUse: Returning learner with a diagnosed error pattern. Leads the lesson: names the specific misconception + the fix. Driven by the item bank's misconception tags.

dueChecklist.whenToUse: When spaced-repetition items are due. Turns review into an actionable checklist.

accuracyStat.whenToUse: Almost always. The 6-session trend + numeric %. Color is never the only signal — the number is always shown.

selfExplainPrompt.whenToUse: Consolidation. Prompt the learner to explain in their own words BEFORE any instructional explanation (self-explanation effect).

coachEntry.whenToUse: Hand-off to the responsive Socratic coach — complements the static lesson scaffold.

newSkill.label: New skill
newSkill.reason: First exposure → teach forward: rule → worked model → a faded try → self-explain. Ends on a win.

returning.label: Returning & struggling
returning.reason: Mastery 49%, 4 misses due → lead with the misconception, clear the due items; rule as backup; coach on hand.

refresher.label: Quick refresher
refresher.reason: High mastery, a pre-drill glance → annotated example + rule, then straight to accuracy.

runtime.composer: Given { skill, learnerContext }, resolve context → ordered block list; partition by `zone` (main | rail); render each block via registry[type]. Unknown types are skipped. `--accent` = skill bucket token.
runtime.selection: In production, the context is not a preset name but a decision from learner state (mastery, recent misconception tags, due schedule) — the same signals the v2 outer loop uses. Presets here are the demonstrable form.
